criterion: Would a plausible rewrite of application code make this assertion catch a mistake? A surviving mutation alone does not justify deletion.
evidence_notes: Identifiers refer to the baseline, including removed or renamed tests and original source lines. Baseline assertion excerpts are not descriptions of repaired assertions. Keep decisions are static contract reviews unless explicit mutation evidence is recorded; shared file-level risks are not bespoke mutation proof. Temporary log paths identify local experiments and are not portable artifacts; their outcomes are summarized here. Live gate outcomes are recorded in docs/test-review.md. Raw URLs inside assertion evidence are omitted: these are fixture examples, not navigable application links. The baseline test identifier locates their exact source.

differs from its field's PLACEHOLDER, not merely from the model default,

apps/purchasing/tests/test_allocations_a.behaviour: no statement locks a row
apps/purchasing/tests/test_allocations_a.rewrite_risk: A GET must not take a row lock, and the SQL is the only honest witness. ``select_for_update`` is legal inside a transaction and raises ``TransactionManagementError`` in autocommit. There is no ``ATOMIC_REQUESTS`` in ``config/``, so locking here is a 500 in production — yet every test in this file passes, because pytest wraps each one in a transaction. The usual escape, ``django_db(transaction=True)``, is closed on purpose: this project refuses Django's ``flush`` (ADR 0048), which that mode needs for teardown. So the request is made normally and the emitted SQL is inspected instead, which pins the property rather than the symptom. Changing allocation ownership, reversal idempotence, receipt remainder or provenance rules loses inventory/job evidence or receives/reverses the same material twice.
